summary: One-time cleanup of the untouched legacy default project (older desktop builds created default_project, ten world-model seed papers and an automatic fetch on first launch). app/legacy_cleanup.py runs once, only from the desktop start-up (app/desktop.py after the instance lock, PDH_APP_VERSION set) or a source run with PDH_LEGACY_CLEANUP=1; build_server does not open the library. Order: commit an in_progress marker, write and verify a uniquely named backup (separate connection, quick_check, row counts, marker present), then in one transaction re-check, delete and set the final marker. Cleans only when nothing was ever done in the project; any doubt keeps everything. Independent-review fixes: marker before backup, verified unique backup, profile-version kinds, language policy, AI previews / weekly AI analysis, multi-day batches, shared papers, desktop-only trigger, exploration evidence and other projects' category entries.
scope_note: Worktree onboarding-tour, fifth commit. Deletes user-library data, hence critical; the conditions are deliberately conservative.

budget_impact.rationale: Local SQLite work at start-up; no model call, network request or prompt.
budget_impact.before: an untouched legacy default project and seed papers stayed in the library
budget_impact.after: removed once, with a backup file

open_risks: Not independently reviewed after the review fixes (critical class; it deletes data).
Not run on the owner's real old library; tests use a state reconstructed from the old migration and ensure_seed_papers.

The verified backup <db>.pre-legacy-cleanup-<time>-<id>.bak is never deleted automatically and holds the old data; restore = copy it over the database (it carries the in_progress marker, so it is not cleaned again).
Conservative by design: a library where anything was touched is left as it is; the owner may delete it by hand.
Cross-branch: after the cleanup, opening the same real library with an old main / v0.1.0 build creates a UUID default project and seeds it again; do not mix builds on one data directory.
Relies on table names and the old first-start shape (default_project, seed_keys_/last_refresh_ settings, profile version note 'initial'); an unknown state is kept (safe direction).
review_notes: Second independent review (after 414b513): mergeable; fixed in the follow-up commit: any second batch (same day included) keeps the project, unexpected stored-data shapes keep everything (recorded, not re-run), an interrupted in_progress run only drops its temporary copy. 39 cleanup tests, full suite OK.
